cd-teepeota-townsite-1856.st: SECOND SOURCE (Wabasha Herald, 19 Oct 1893, 'An Old Timer'): A. B. Roe, a builder who put up nearly every building in Teepeota in 1857-59, revisited the site, found the old streets and building spots, and traced the old steamboat landing. 'Naught but slight depressions in the earth, where once were cellars' remained. The March 1859 fire, set on purpose, destroyed everything except Roe's house and one other building; Roe sold to Seth Tennee. Roe's surviving house was then Henry L. Feddern's residence (correction, Herald 26 Oct 1893). 1899-1900 river-improvement reports still name a 'Teepeota' shoal. The 1896 Wabasha plat should show the Feddern place by the river; the townsite and landing were next to it.
src: Wabasha Herald, 19 Oct 1893 p3 (MNHS Newspaper Hub)
